**Refined prompt:** Enumerate every HTTP route in this NestJS RealWorld API that is reachable without a valid JWT, answering from the actual `configure()` middleware registrations rather than from decorators or Swagger annotations, with each claim cited to file:line — and flag any route that is public but shouldn't be.

Auth here is per-route `AuthMiddleware` registered in each module's `configure()`. There is no global guard (`ApplicationModule` at `src/app.module.ts:23` has no `configure()`), so **a route is public unless it is named in one of those blocks**. Only three modules register anything: `src/user/user.module.ts:20`, `src/article/article.module.ts:24-31`, `src/profile/profile.module.ts:22`. `TagModule`'s `configure()` is empty (`src/tag/tag.module.ts:17-18`).

Cross-referencing that against every declared handler, nine routes are callable with no token (global prefix `api`, `src/main.ts:8`):

| Route | Handler | Intended public? |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/` | `src/app.controller.ts:5` | Yes — "Hello World!" stub |
| `POST /api/users` | `src/user/user.controller.ts:32` | Yes — register |
| `POST /api/users/login` | `src/user/user.controller.ts:43` | Yes — login |
| **`DELETE /api/users/:slug`** | `src/user/user.controller.ts:37` | **No — see below** |
| `GET /api/articles` | `src/article/article.controller.ts:24` | Yes |
| `GET /api/articles/:slug` | `src/article/article.controller.ts:38` | Yes |
| `GET /api/articles/:slug/comments` | `src/article/article.controller.ts:43` | Yes |
| `GET /api/profiles/:username` | `src/profile/profile.controller.ts:18` | Yes |
| `GET /api/tags` | `src/tag/tag.controller.ts:17` | Yes |

Eight of these are the RealWorld spec's public surface. One is not.

## `DELETE /api/users/:slug` deletes any account, unauthenticated

`src/user/user.controller.ts:37-39` passes `params.slug` straight into `UserService.delete()`, which at `src/user/user.service.ts:83-84` is `this.userRepository.delete({ email: email })` — the param is matched against the **email** column. So `DELETE /api/users/victim@example.com` deletes that user, with no token, no ownership check, and no rate limit. It isn't in `UserModule`'s middleware list, which only covers `GET /user` and `PUT /user`.

This is the one finding worth acting on. The other eight are correct by spec.

## Two caveats on the "public" column

**Public ≠ anonymous.** `@User('id')` works without the middleware — on a tokenless route it decodes the header itself (`src/user/user.decorator.ts:13-17`) and returns `undefined` if absent. `GET /api/profiles/:username` relies on this (`src/profile/profile.controller.ts:19`) for optional identity. That's deliberate.

**Public routes can still 500.** That same decoder calls `jwt.verify` uncaught at `src/user/user.decorator.ts:15`, as does the middleware at `src/user/auth.middleware.ts:17`. An expired or tampered token sent to a *public* route throws a framework 500 rather than being ignored — LESSONS.md #79, still unfixed.

Worth noting the near-miss: `GET /articles/feed` *is* guarded, and it survives only because `getFeed()` (line 33) is declared above `findOne()` (`:slug`, line 38). Were that order reversed, an unauthenticated `/articles/feed` would fall through to the public `:slug` handler and silently bypass the guard. That ordering was fixed previously (LESSONS.md #7).

**Not read:** the article/profile/tag service bodies (I only needed the route registrations plus `UserService.delete`), and the `prisma/` folder, which `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:23-24` marks as a parallel experiment rather than the production path.

Ownership checks on the *guarded* mutating routes are a separate and also-missing concern — `PUT`/`DELETE /articles/:slug` authenticate but never compare caller to author. That's already tracked as in-flight work in `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:10-12`, so I've left it out of scope here. Want me to draft the fix for the unauthenticated delete?
